technical_and_design_decisions: For U1 and U2, refactoring of the statebased and entities packages will replace internal fabric utility usage with standalone or standard library implementations, ensuring only fabric protobuf packages remain as fabric imports to meet acceptance criteria.

For U5-U8, each requested component (protoutil, BCCSP, MSP, discovery client) will be extracted into a separate, versioned Go module under the fabric-lib-go repository, with unnecessary internal fabric dependencies removed and public APIs maintained for backward compatibility with downstream SDK users.

For U3 and U4, the marbles02_private tutorial fix will be applied directly to the example chaincode export commands and associated documentation in the fabric-samples repository, adding the tr -d \ step to strip newline characters from base64-encoded JSON inputs.

All refactoring and externalization work will be validated using existing component test suites and dependency checks (via go list) to confirm no unintended fabric dependencies remain in modified packages, and that externalized modules have no unnecessary internal dependencies.
assumptions: Existing test suites for all affected components (statebased, entities, protoutil, BCCSP, MSP, discovery client) are available and pass prior to changes, and can be used to validate that refactoring/externalization does not break existing functionality.
The fabric-protos-go module is already published and available as a public dependency, so no work is required to externalize protobuf definitions as part of this increment.
The marbles02_private chaincode example and its associated tutorial documentation are hosted in the public fabric-samples repository and can be modified directly as part of this increment.
No functional changes to the externalized components are required, only extraction into standalone modules and removal of unnecessary internal dependencies.
No SDK migration work is included in scope; existing SDK consumers will be responsible for migrating to the new standalone externalized modules on their own timeline.
All new externalized modules will be published to the public Go module proxy under the github.com/hyperledger organization, with no additional infrastructure work required.
